questions.q: What is the difference between a class and an object?
options: A class is the blueprint (Product); an object is one thing made from it (masala), with its own data
An object is a blueprint for classes
A class is a kind of dict
questions.explain: One class, many objects. masala and earbuds are both Products, each with its own stock.

options: Every time a method is called
Automatically, each time you make a new object, like Product("Masala Box", 29900, ...)
Only if you call obj.__init__() yourself
questions.explain: The arguments you pass to Product(...) go to __init__, which stores them on the new object.

questions.q: In masala.sell(2), what is self inside sell?
options: masala, the object before the dot
questions.explain: masala.sell(2) is short for Product.sell(masala, 2). Python passes the object as self.

questions.q: Why is a Product class safer than a product dict?
options: __init__ can refuse bad data (like a price of "cheap"), so a broken product can never exist
questions.explain: A dict accepts anything. A class checks its data the moment the object is made, and keeps the rules next to the data.

questions.q: class Cart: lines = [] (outside __init__). Asha's and Ravi's carts both show both customers' items. Why?
options: lines is a class attribute: ONE list shared by every Cart
The customers have the same name
questions.explain: Neither cart has its own lines, so self.lines finds the class's list. Fix: self.lines = [] inside __init__.

questions.q: def label(): return "Product" inside the class, then masala.label(). What happens?
options: TypeError: Product.label() takes 0 positional arguments but 1 was given
questions.explain: Python always passes the object as the first argument. Every method needs self as its first parameter.

questions.q: (Going deeper) Where does an object keep its attributes?
options: In a dict, obj.__dict__ (vars(obj) shows it)
questions.explain: Reading masala.x looks in the object's own dict first, then in the class. That's why self.lines found the class's shared list.

questions.q: (Going deeper) Is a class attribute ever a good idea?
options: Yes, for values every object shares and nobody changes through an object, like CURRENCY = "INR"
questions.explain: Shared constants are fine. Changeable values (lists, dicts) on the class are the trap.
